shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading 1×A for 1×B would just swap which good has 0, since I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of all three goods. This would make my bundle 1C/0A/2B, decreasing variety and not improving utility. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade to acquire a good I lack, not create a new deficiency.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of C, A, B. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and utility. Better to keep balanced holdings.

Current inventory is 1 C, 1 A, 1 B - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating a lopsided bundle (missing a good entirely). Since I value variety, this would decrease my utility despite gaining quantity in A.
Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly even. Trading away my only C for another B would make me 0 C, 1 A, 2 B, which is less diverse and reduces utility since I value variety. No net gain.
This trade would give me 2C/1A/0B, making my bundle less diverse (moving from 1/1/1 to 2/1/0) and reducing utility since I value variety. I should decline this offer.

This trade would leave me with 3 C, 1 A, 0 B - reducing variety since I'd lose my only B, going to zero in that good while stacking up C. Since I value variety, this would decrease my utility rather than increase it.
Current inventory is 1 each of C, A, B - perfectly balanced. Trading away A for B would just shift the imbalance (0 A, 2 B) without improving variety, so utility would not increase.
Current inventory is 1 each of C, A, B - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another A would make me 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, which is less varied and reduces utility since I value variety.

Current inventory is C:1, A:1, B:1 - a balanced bundle I value for its variety. Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with C:1, A:3, B:0, creating a lopsided bundle with zero B, which reduces variety value even though total goods increase. Better to seek a trade that maintains or improves variety instead of eliminating a good entirely.

I currently have equal amounts of C, A, and B (1 each). Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would hurt my balanced holdings.

This trade would give me 2×C and 0×B, moving away from variety (1,1,1) toward an imbalanced bundle. Since I value variety, having equal amounts of C, A, B is preferable; trading away my only B for a second C reduces utility.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Accepting would give me 3 C, 1 A, 0 B — losing my only B and creating a heavy imbalance, which hurts my variety-based utility more than gaining extra C helps.

Currently I have C:1, A:2, B:0 - very unbalanced. Trading away 1 A (which I have surplus of) for 1 B (which I have none of) improves variety: resulting in C:1, A:1, B:1, a perfectly balanced bundle. This increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, trading a good I have some of for still-scarce variety but at a steep 2-for-1 rate. Current inventory C1/A2/B0 - I'd rather trade 1A for 1B to balance toward C1/A1/B1, which maximizes variety. This trade over-concentrates the cost on my A holdings and leaves me with too few goods overall (1C+1B=2 total vs giving up 2A). Better to negotiate a 1-for-1 swap instead.

I currently have C:1, A:2, B:0. Trading my only C for a B gives me C:0, A:2, B:1, moving toward a more even distribution (0,2,1) vs (1,2,0) - similar variance but B was completely absent, so gaining my first B unit has high marginal value while losing my only C reduces it to zero. Since I value variety, having some of each good is generally better; however this trade eliminates C entirely while giving B. Given diminishing returns favor filling empty slots, moving from (1,2,0) to (0,2,1) keeps one good at zero either way, but B was more scarce (0) than C (1), so acquiring B has higher marginal utility than the C I give up.
Trading 1 A (of which I have 2) for 1 B (of which I have 0) moves my inventory toward a more even distribution (C1, A1, B1), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up both my A for only 1 B would leave me with 1C, 0A, 1B - trading a scarce good imbalance for another. I'd end up with 0 of A, which hurts variety. Better to give only 1 A for 1 B to balance my bundle (1C,1A,1B), so this exact trade is unfavorable.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just swapping which good I lack instead of improving variety. Current bundle is C:1, A:2, B:0 - after trade it'd be C:0, A:2, B:1, which doesn't increase diversity since I still have a zero. Better to seek a trade that adds B without fully depleting C.

Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility since I'd go from a balanced 1-1-0 bundle to an unbalanced 0-2-0 bundle (with C still at 0). This doesn't improve my diversified holdings.

This trade would give me 2×A and 0×B, moving from a balanced (1,1,0) bundle to a more skewed (2,0,0) bundle. Since I value variety, this reduces utility rather than improving it. I'd prefer to acquire C instead, or a trade that doesn't unbalance my A/B holdings.

Current inventory is C:0, A:1, B:1. Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with C:0, A:3, B:0, which is heavily imbalanced and eliminates variety entirely (losing B and having no C). Given I value variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than improving it. I'd prefer to acquire C or keep balanced holdings across all three goods.

Currently I have C:0, A:1, B:1. Trading away my only B for C would just swap which good I have zero of, resulting in C:1, A:1, B:0 - no improvement in variety. Since I value variety, this trade doesn't increase my utility.

Current inventory: A=1, B=1, C=0. Giving up my only B for 2C would leave me with C=2, A=1, B=0, losing variety in B entirely. Since I value variety, going from having 1 of each (missing only C) to having 0 B and 2 C is not clearly better - I'd rather trade for C without giving up my only B. I'd prefer a deal like giving A (which I also only have 1 of) or finding a trade that keeps some balance, or getting C without fully depleting B."

Currently I have C:1, A:1, B:0. Trading my extra A for B gives me one of each good (C:1, A:0, B:1), achieving perfect variety across all three goods, which maximizes utility under my preference for variety.

Currently I have 1C, 1A, 0B. Trading 1C for 1B gives me 0C, 1A, 1B - same total variety spread but now I'd have zero of C. Actually, let me reconsider: going from (1,1,0) to (0,1,1) just shifts which good I lack, not a net improvement since both have one good at zero. However, since C would drop to 0 and B rises to 1, the marginal utility of gaining a first unit of B (currently valued highly since I have none) exceeds losing my only C (dropping to zero, which is symmetric). Since this is a lateral move with equal counts of scarce goods, I'll accept to diversify toward a more balanced future trading position and enable further trades using B as leverage.

Currently I have C:2, A:1, B:0. Trading away my only A for B would just swap which good I have zero of, going from (2,1,0) to (2,0,1), which doesn't improve variety balance. I'd rather keep A and acquire B without giving up my only A, or get B while keeping some A.

Current inventory is C:2, A:1, B:0 - highly imbalanced. Trading away a C (which I have 2 of) for a B (which I have none of) improves variety and balances my bundle toward C:1, A:1, B:1, which is ideal given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 C for only 1 B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 1 B - trading away all of one good is too extreme. I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade to balance my inventory (2 C, 1 A, 0 B) without depleting C entirely.

Currently I only have C (1 unit) and nothing else. Trading 1 C for 1 B gives me a more diverse bundle (0 C, 1 B) instead of concentrated in C, which better serves my variety preference since I have less B than C currently.
Currently I have C:1, A:2, B:0 - very unbalanced. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to C:1, A:1, B:1, a perfectly balanced bundle, which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

This would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, going from a balanced 1C/2A/0B to 1C/0A/1B - trading two units of A for just one B is too steep a ratio and would leave me with zero A, hurting variety. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead.

Trading my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just swapping scarcity from B to C without improving variety. I'd end up with C:0, A:2, B:1 - still uneven and I lose my only unit of C. Better to seek a trade that doesn't zero out a good I only have one of, or get something that improves balance without eliminating C entirely.
Currently I have only A (1) and nothing else. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me one of each of A and B, improving variety and balance, which increases my utility under variety-preferring preferences.
